Package io.github.mikestitt.corbelsflightlog.ftc

Class FtcFlightLog

java.lang.Object
io.github.mikestitt.corbelsflightlog.ftc.FtcFlightLog
All Implemented Interfaces:
com.qualcomm.robotcore.eventloop.opmode.OpModeManagerNotifier.Notifications
public final class FtcFlightLog extends Object implements com.qualcomm.robotcore.eventloop.opmode.OpModeManagerNotifier.Notifications
FlightLog for an FTC robot: files land in the Robot Controller's own storage, are named after the OpMode, and are closed when the OpMode stops -- whether or not your code remembers to. 
 private FlightLog log;

 public void start() { log = FtcFlightLog.open(this); }
 public void loop()  { log.recordOutput("shooter/rpm", rpm); log.endLoop(); }
 public void stop()  { log.close(); }   // optional: see below

Closing. This registers with the Robot Controller and closes the open log when an OpMode stops, and again before the next one initialises. So a log survives an OpMode that throws, or that never calls close(). Calling close() yourself still works and is still worth doing: it flushes immediately rather than at the end of the OpMode.

Where the files go. logDirectory() is a corbelsflightlog folder at the top of the Robot Controller's storage -- the SDK's AppUtil.ROOT_FOLDER, so /sdcard/corbelsflightlog, which is internal storage on a Control Hub, not a removable card. If that folder can't be used, this falls back to a corbelsflightlog folder in the app's private files directory, which always exists.

Getting them off the robot. With the laptop on the robot's Wi-Fi, open 192.168.43.1:8080/corbelsflightlog and click a file. adb pull still works too.

    • openLive

      public static FlightLog openLive(com.qualcomm.robotcore.eventloop.opmode.OpMode opMode)
      Opens a log as open(OpMode) does, and sends every value it records live to AdvantageScope as well, over NetworkTables 4 at 192.168.43.1:5810. The server starts on the first call and runs until the Robot Controller app stops.

      For practice only. FTC rule R704 forbids third-party telemetry over Wi-Fi at competitions, so a competition OpMode calls open(com.qualcomm.robotcore.eventloop.opmode.OpMode). If the server cannot start, the log still records and the reason goes to the robot's log.
